name: walkers_guide_a
prompt:
Two images are attached.
Image 1 is finished art from the same game, cars seen from above. Match its painting style, finish and light only — not its contents, colours or scale.
Image 2 is a pose guide: 40 stick figures in exactly the grid this sheet must have, 8 columns by 5 rows. In it the blue limbs are the person's LEFT leg and arm, the red limbs their RIGHT leg and arm, and the black dot is the nose. Draw the person in each cell in exactly the pose of the stick figure in the same cell: the same leg in front, the same arm swung forward, facing the same way. Take nothing else from it: no sticks, no blue or red, no dots, no grey background, and not its thin proportions.

Make one image: a walking-animation sprite sheet for a 2D city game, of one person walking. Lay it as a grid of 8 columns by 5 rows, exactly as image 2, 40 figures in all, each standing in its own equal cell, well apart from its neighbours: no figure touches or overlaps another, and nothing reaches into the next cell. All 40 figures are the same person.

The view is the same for every figure: from in front of the person and high above, looking down at about 40 degrees, as in a classic top-down role-playing game — the top of the head and the shoulders show, the whole body is seen, a little shortened, the feet at the bottom. Each figure stands upright on its feet; the ground is not drawn.

Rows — the way the person walks, the same in every column of a row:
1. Straight away from us, up the picture: we see the back of the head, the back and the backs of the legs.
2. Diagonally away and to the left, towards the top-left corner: we see the back and the left side; the face is turned away.
3. To the left: the left side in profile, the nose pointing left.
4. Diagonally towards us and to the left, towards the bottom-left corner: we see the front and the left side, the face in three-quarter view looking down-left.
5. Straight towards us, down the picture: we see the face and the front.
Nobody in rows 2 to 4 faces or walks to the right.

Columns — two steps of one walk, in order, as the guide's columns show. Both legs walk: the leg in front changes from step to step.
1. Standing, feet side by side, arms at the sides.
2. Left leg swinging forward.
3. Full stride, left leg in front, right arm forward.
4. Weight on the left leg, right foot lifting behind.
5. Passing: right foot swinging past the left.
6. Right leg swinging forward.
7. Full stride, right leg in front, left arm forward.
8. Weight on the right leg, left foot lifting behind.

Every figure of one person is the same person: the same height, build, face, hair, clothes, colours and anything carried. All the figures of a person are the same size: the head at the same height and the feet on one line in every cell of a row. Between cells only the facing, the legs and the arms change. The stride is a calm walk, not a run, but plainly a walk: at a full stride the feet are a foot's length or more apart, and the arms swing clearly, opposite to the legs.

A real adult in natural proportions: the head about one seventh of the height, slim natural limbs — not a chibi, not a big-headed cartoon.

Style: painted game art like the style image — soft detailed painting, a clean readable silhouette, a thin darker edge rather than a heavy black outline, natural believable colours, light from the top-left with soft shading on the figure. Summer in a Black Sea port city.

Everything outside the figures is fully transparent: no background colour, no ground, no floor line, no cast shadow, nothing half-transparent. No text, letters, numbers, labels, grid lines, frames or borders anywhere.

The person: 1.84 m tall. A grey-haired man of about 60, clean-shaven, in a light-brown linen jacket worn open over a cream shirt, dark-grey trousers and brown leather shoes.
